header: The server side of the employee manager (step 66a): it gives the one-word decision the omnibar needs ("is this person allowed to open the manager?"). The database connection and the logged-in person are the PAX editor's (src/lib/pax/admin/access.ts): I use the application's OWN connection, never the language model's read-only client, and the ticket from the login session, never anything typed.

symbols.name: typeormEmpDb
doc: This is the employee manager's database: the application's own connection, in a transaction per request. I carry the connection as its KEY (step 67d), so that the store can remember the table layout and the code lists for a few minutes per database: a new wrapper is made for every request, and the connection is the one thing that stays.

symbols.name: authorityForTicket
symbols.sig: export async function authorityForTicket(ds: DataSource, ticket: string | null | undefined): Promise<Authority | null>
doc: Returns HOD, delegate, or null for this ticket. A failing read means null: I never open the manager on doubt.
